explanation.text:
(Pro. 18:1-24)

Through desire . . . seeketh--that is, seeks selfish gratification.

intermeddleth . . . wisdom--or, "rushes on" (Pro 17:14) against all wisdom, or what is valuable (Pro 2:7).

bsb.text: He who isolates himself pursues selfish desires; he rebels against all sound judgment.

explanation.text: that his heart . . . itself--that is, takes pleasure in revealing his folly (Pro 12:23; Pro 15:2).

bsb.text: A fool does not delight in understanding, but only in airing his opinions.

explanation.text:
So surely are sin and punishment connected (Pro 16:4).

wicked, for "wickedness," answers to

ignominy, or the state of such; and

contempt, the feeling of others to them; and to

reproach, a manifestation of contempt.

bsb.text: With a wicked man comes contempt as well, and shame is accompanied by disgrace.

explanation.text: Wise speech is like an exhaustless stream of benefit.

bsb.text: The words of a man’s mouth are deep waters; the fountain of wisdom is a bubbling brook.

explanation.text: accept the person--(Compare Psa 82:2). "It is not good" is to be supplied before "to overthrow."

bsb.text: Showing partiality to the wicked is not good, nor is depriving the innocent of justice.

explanation.text: The quarrelsome bring trouble on themselves. Their rash language ensnares them (Pro 6:2).

bsb.text: A fool’s lips bring him strife, and his mouth invites a beating.

explanation.text:
A fool's mouth is his destruction,.... The cause of it; for his contentions, and quarrels, and evil speaking, lawsuits are commenced against him, which bring ruin upon himself and his family now; as well as for his idle and wicked words he will be condemned hereafter, Matthew 12:35; there is a world of iniquity in the mouth and tongue of a wicked man, which bring destruction upon himself and others, James 3:6;

and his lips are the snare of his soul; from speaking in his own defence, he says things which should not be said, and by which he is entangled yet more and more; he is caught by his own words and condemned by them; or his loquacity, in which he delights, is a snare unto him to say things which neither become him, nor are for his advantage, but the contrary; see Proverbs 12:13.

bsb.text: A fool’s mouth is his ruin, and his lips are a snare to his soul.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 16:28).

as wounds--not sustained by the Hebrew; better, as "sweet morsels," which men gladly swallow.

innermost . . . belly--the mind, or heart (compare Pro 20:27-30; Psa 22:14).

bsb.text: The words of a gossip are like choice morsels that go down into the inmost being.

explanation.text:
One by failing to get, the other by wasting wealth, grows poor.

waster--literally, "master of washing," a prodigal.

bsb.text: Whoever is slothful in his work is brother to him who destroys.

explanation.text:
name of the Lord--manifested perfections (Psa 8:1; Psa 20:2), as faithfulness, power, mercy, etc., on which men rely.

is safe--literally, "set on high, out of danger" (Psa 18:2; Psa 91:4).

bsb.text: The name of the LORD is a strong tower; the righteous run to it and are safe.

explanation.text: contrasts with Pro 18:10 (compare Pro 10:15). Such is a vain trust (compare Psa 73:6).

bsb.text: A rich man’s wealth is his fortified city; it is like a high wall in his imagination.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 15:33; Pro 16:18).

bsb.text: Before his downfall a man’s heart is proud, but humility comes before honor.

explanation.text: Hasty speech evinces self-conceit, and ensures shame (Pro 26:12).

bsb.text: He who answers a matter before he hears it—this is folly and disgrace to him.

explanation.text: infirmity--bodily sickness, or outward evil. The spirit, which sustains, being wounded, no support is left, except, as implied, in God.

bsb.text: The spirit of a man can endure his sickness, but who can survive a broken spirit?

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 1:5, Pro 1:15, Pro 1:31).

bsb.text: The heart of the discerning acquires knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeks it out.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 17:8, Pro 17:23). Disapproval of the fact stated is implied.

bsb.text: A man’s gift opens doors for him, and brings him before great men.

explanation.text:
One-sided statements are not reliable.

searcheth--thoroughly (Pro 17:9, Pro 17:19).

bsb.text: The first to state his case seems right until another comes and cross-examines him.

explanation.text: The lot--whose disposal is of God (Pro 16:13), may, properly used, be a right mode of settling disputes.

bsb.text: Casting the lot ends quarrels and separates strong opponents.

explanation.text: No feuds so difficult of adjustment as those of relatives; hence great care should be used to avoid them.

bsb.text: An offended brother is harder to win than a fortified city, and disputes are like the bars of a castle.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 12:14; Pro 13:2). Men's words are the fruit, or, increase of his lips, and when good, benefit them.

satisfied with--(Compare Pro 1:31; Pro 14:14).

bsb.text: From the fruit of his mouth a man’s belly is filled; with the harvest from his lips he is satisfied.

explanation.text:
Death and life--or, the greatest evil and good.

that love it--that is, the tongue, or its use for good or evil.

eat . . . fruit--(Compare Pro 18:19; Jam 1:19).

bsb.text: Life and death are in the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruit.

explanation.text: The old versions supply "good" before the "wife," as the last clause and Pro 19:14 imply (compare Pro 31:10).

bsb.text: He who finds a wife finds a good thing and obtains favor from the LORD.

explanation.text: the rich . . . roughly--He is tolerated because rich, implying that the estimate of men by wealth is wrong.

bsb.text: The poor man pleads for mercy, but the rich man answers harshly.

explanation.text:
A man . . . friendly--better, "A man . . . (is) to, or, may triumph (Psa 108:9), or, shout for joy (Psa 5:11), that is, may congratulate himself." Indeed, there is a Friend who is better than a brother; such is the "Friend of sinners" [Mat 11:19; Luk 7:34], who may have been before the writer's mind.

Next: Proverbs Chapter 19

bsb.text: A man of many companions may come to ruin, but there is a friend who stays closer than a brother.
